title: Installable and honestly offline
summary: Ship a web app manifest and a service worker whose cache strategy matches each request.

scenario.briefing: The campus app offers an install button on some browsers and shows a blank page when the network drops. The manifest is incomplete, every response is cached under one name, and API calls are stored beside public assets. Build a versioned worker that pre-caches the shell, falls back to an offline document for navigations, and leaves private requests alone.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Start with a cache version and derive both cache names from it.
Pre-cache the manifest, icons, and offline page during install and pass the promise to waitUntil.
Skip non-GET, cross-origin, and /api/ requests before choosing a strategy.
Return the cached asset immediately, refresh it in the background, and use offline.html for failed navigations.

misconceptions.description: Caching every response, including authenticated API calls.
misconceptions.feedback: Private responses can be replayed to another user on a shared device. Skip /api/ or cache only explicitly public responses.

misconceptions.description: Reusing one cache name across releases.
misconceptions.feedback: Old shell assets survive the deploy. Version the cache name and delete stale caches on activate.
The browser may terminate the worker before the cache is filled. Pass the promise to waitUntil.

sections.title: A manifest makes installation possible
sections.body: Installability needs more than a registered worker. The manifest supplies the app name, start URL, standalone display mode, theme colors, and at least 192px and 512px icons. Browsers still vary, but a complete manifest over HTTPS is the common baseline.

sections.title: The lifecycle is install, activate, fetch
sections.body: install fills the shell cache, activate removes caches from earlier releases and claims clients, and fetch chooses a strategy per request. Work started during install must be passed to event.waitUntil or the browser can stop the worker before the cache is ready.

sections.title: Version the caches, not just the files
sections.body: Derive every cache name from a version string and delete every cache that does not match during activate. Reusing one name across deploys leaves old shell files in place, and a changed index.html can reference assets that were never cached.

sections.title: Stale-while-revalidate is a trade
sections.body: Return the stored response immediately while a network request refreshes it in the background. The screen is fast and can be one deploy behind. This is acceptable for public assets and wrong for authenticated API responses.

sections.title: Offline fallback is a route
sections.body: A failed navigation should resolve to a cached offline document instead of a rejected promise. API calls should fail visibly so the interface can offer a retry rather than replay private data from another session.

vocabulary.definition: A JSON document that names the app, its start URL, display mode, colors, and icons so a browser can offer installation.
A background script that intercepts network requests for its origin and can serve cached responses.
A cache strategy that returns the stored response immediately and refreshes it from the network in the background.
A label in the cache name that lets activate delete assets from earlier releases.

steps.title: Write a versioned service worker with an offline fallback
steps.prompt: Edit service-worker.ts. Add a versioned shell cache and runtime cache, pre-cache the manifest, icons, and offline page during install, delete stale caches during activate, serve navigations from the network with an offline fallback, and use stale-while-revalidate for same-origin GET assets. Skip non-GET, cross-origin, and /api/ requests.

tests.description: Both caches carry the same version and stale caches are deleted.
Navigations fall back to the offline document and API requests are skipped.
Assets use stale-while-revalidate and the starter marker is gone.

steps.title: Manifest, lifecycle, and cache policy

statements.label: A manifest with a name, start URL, standalone display, and 192px and 512px icons is part of the installability contract.
install fills the cache, activate cleans old caches, and fetch serves requests.
Including a version in the cache name and deleting stale caches on activate prevents old shell files from surviving a deploy.
Authenticated API responses should be cached by default so every screen works offline.
A failed navigation should resolve to a cached offline document instead of a rejected fetch.
Registering a service worker alone makes an app installable without a manifest.

steps.explanation: The manifest describes the installed app and the worker controls what loads offline. A versioned shell cache plus cleanup on activate keeps releases separate, and per-request strategies keep private responses out of shared caches.
